tools.name: BackgroundTask
tools.description: Launch a background agent for long-running work that shouldn't block the conversation. Use for large-scale analysis, multi-file refactoring, or operations that may take minutes. Returns immediately with an agent_id and output_file path. Use TaskOutput(agent_id, action='result') to retrieve output, or Read the output_file directly for a live view while running. Do not duplicate the agent's work on the same files while it is running.

agent_id.description: Optional custom ID for tracking this background agent. If omitted, an ID will be auto-generated.

model.description: Optional model to use for the background agent.

resume.description: Optional agent_id of a prior BackgroundTask run to resume.

system_prompt.description: Optional custom system prompt for the background agent.

task.description: The long-running task for the background agent to perform.

tools.description: Optional list of tool names the background agent can use. If omitted, the agent has access to all available tools.

tools.name: Delegate
tools.description: Spawn a focused agent that can ask the parent clarifying questions. Use DelegateOutput to poll, answer questions, check status, and retrieve the result; use Subagent instead for fully autonomous work.

agent_id.description: Agent type to invoke (e.g. 'general-assistant', 'research-agent'). Defaults to general-assistant.

inherit_context.description: If true, the delegate receives your conversation summary and tool set as additional context.

model.description: Optional model override for the delegate (e.g. 'sonnet', 'haiku').

system_prompt.description: Custom system prompt for the delegate. Overrides agent_id configuration.

task.description: The specific task to delegate. Be clear and self-contained — the delegate agent will work autonomously but can ask you questions.

tools.name: DelegateOutput
tools.description:
Interact with an active delegate agent spawned by Delegate().

Actions:
  "status"  — Check current state, pending questions, and task progress.
  "poll"    — Wait up to 10s for a question from the delegate or completion.
              Use this to efficiently wait for questions without busy-looping.
  "answer"  — Send your answer to a pending question. The delegate resumes immediately.
  "result"  — Read the delegate's final output. Use offset for incremental reads.
  "cancel"  — Cancel a running delegate.

Typical polling loop:
  while true:
    out = DelegateOutput(agent_id, "poll")
    if out has question → DelegateOutput(agent_id, "answer", "your answer")
    if out.status == "done" → DelegateOutput(agent_id, "result") and break

Pass offset from a previous 'result' call to read only new content.

action.description: Action: 'status' (current state + pending questions), 'poll' (wait briefly for a question or completion), 'answer' (send answer to delegate), 'result' (get final output), 'cancel' (stop the delegate)

agent_id.description: The delegate agent_id returned by Delegate()

answer.description: Your answer to the delegate's question. Used with action='answer'.

offset.description: Byte offset for incremental result reads. Use new_offset from a previous result call.

question_id.description: The question_id from the pending question. Used with action='answer' for precision (optional — omit to answer the current pending question).

tools.name: HistoryGet
tools.description: Read a bounded excerpt from one prior conversation selected with HistorySearch. Defaults to the current workspace — just pass conversation_id. If the conversation lives in another project (e.g. it came from a scope=all search) OR the user explicitly asks to read across projects, set all_workspaces=true to read it by ID regardless of directory. You do NOT need to pass workspace_path; that is an advanced exact-path override. Returns message IDs, roles, timestamps, and truncation provenance.

all_workspaces.description: Read the conversation by ID regardless of which workspace it belongs to. Use this when the ID came from a scope=all search or the user asks to read across projects. Preferred over passing workspace_path.

human_only.description: Omit system/tool messages and machine-only reminder boilerplate.

offset.description: Zero-based start position in the original stored message sequence. Uses max_messages as the page size. Mutually exclusive with tail.

tail.description: Return the final N stored messages. Mutually exclusive with offset.

workspace_path.description: Advanced: exact absolute workspace path containing the conversation. You normally do not need this — use the current-workspace default or all_workspaces=true. Ignored when all_workspaces=true.

tools.name: HistorySearch
tools.description: Search prior conversations by title, preview, or substantive message text. Defaults to the current workspace (the common case — just pass a query). Set scope="all" to search across every workspace, but only do that when the current workspace has no match or the user explicitly asks to look across projects. You normally do NOT need to pass workspace_path; it is an advanced override for pinning one exact absolute workspace. Returns bounded conversation metadata and provenance, not full transcripts. complete=false and partial_reasons mean the scan hit a resource limit or skipped malformed/oversized records; do not interpret partial results as exhaustive. Use HistoryGet only for selected conversation IDs.

case_sensitive.description: Match case-exactly. Applies to both plain query terms and `regex`. Default false (case-insensitive; the regex is compiled with a leading (?i) so character classes still behave correctly). Set true to distinguish `Error` from `error`, or a Go exported identifier from a local one.

exclude_runtime.description: Ignore runtime-injected pseudo-messages when matching message bodies. A `user` role is NOT proof a human typed it: the runtime injects `<system-reminder`, `[SCHEDULED]`, `## MCP Context`, `## Current Tasks` and `**Current Mode**` blocks into the user turn. Set true when you are looking for something a PERSON actually said and do not want scaffolding boilerplate to match. Same predicate as HistoryGet's human_only.

fields.description: Restrict matching to these fields. Default (omitted) searches all of them, which is today's behavior. Use ["title"] to find conversations ABOUT a topic rather than ones that merely mention it in passing; use ["body"] to find a string that was said mid-conversation. Note `body` is only consulted when search_body is on.

max_snippets.description: Maximum snippets returned per result. Only meaningful with snippet=true.

min_messages.description: Exclude conversations with fewer stored messages.

ngram.description: Phrase length for stats, from 1 to 5. Use 1 for vocabulary; 2 or 3 for useful recurring phrases. Higher values usually produce near-unique strings. Only meaningful with stats=true.

query.description: Case-insensitive title, preview, and message-body query. Empty lists recent conversations.

regex.description: Go RE2 regular expression applied to selected metadata or individual message records, not across record boundaries. Reach for this when a plain query cannot express the shape you want: commit prefixes (`fix\(hooks\):\s+\w+`), identifiers (`PR #\d{3}`), alternation (`panic|fatal error`), or anchors. RE2 syntax only — lookahead and backreferences are NOT supported and return a clear error. Combines with `query`: the query narrows candidates cheaply and the regex then filters them, so both must match. An invalid pattern is reported as an error, never silently ignored.

scope.description: Default "current" searches this workspace. Use "all" only when the current workspace has no match or the user explicitly asks to search across all projects.

search_body.description: Search substantive user/assistant message text in addition to title and preview. Defaults to true when query or regex is non-empty.

segment_kind.description: Filter matches to one segment kind: message prose, tool_call input, or tool_result output.

snippet.description: Return the matching text with surrounding context plus which field matched, instead of only a generic preview. Turn this on whenever you need to know WHY a conversation matched — it is the difference between a list of IDs and actual evidence. Snippets are bounded in length and count and never split a multi-byte character.

snippet_context.description: Bytes of surrounding context on each side of a match in a snippet. Only meaningful with snippet=true.

sort.description: Sort results by relevance, recency, or message count. Defaults to relevance for a query or regex and recency when both are empty.

stats.description: Return a frequency table INSTEAD OF a conversation list. This changes the shape of the output. Use it to study vocabulary or recurring phrasing across many conversations; do not use it when you are trying to find and open one conversation.

tool_name.description: Filter to segments for one tool name, for example "Bash". This matches only tool segments, so setting it searches tool traffic rather than ordinary conversation prose.

tool_outcome.description: Filter tool results by outcome: any, failed, or succeeded. Setting this implies tool-result segments because only tool results have an outcome.

top_terms.description: Maximum frequency rows to return. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 500 because large frequency tables can flood a terminal or model context window. Only meaningful with stats=true.

workspace_path.description: Advanced: exact absolute workspace path to search. You rarely need this — prefer the default current scope, or scope=all. Mutually exclusive with scope=all.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Views an image, SVG or PDF file so you can actually see it.

Supported: .jpg, .jpeg, .png, .gif, .webp (returned as pictures); .svg (returned as
its source text); .pdf (page 1 returned as a picture). Every result ends with a
`Cite as:` line: cite that path, plus `#page=1` for a PDF.

For every other kind of file, use the shell instead:
  - whole file:   cat FILE
  - a slice:      sed -n 'START,ENDp' FILE
  - with numbers: nl -ba FILE | sed -n 'START,ENDp'
  - first/last:   head -n N FILE  /  tail -n N FILE
  - search:       rg PATTERN        (add -n for line numbers, -t go to filter)
  - find files:   rg --files -g 'PATTERN'

file_path.description: Absolute path to the image file (.jpg, .jpeg, .png, .gif, .webp).

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Execute a skill within the main conversation.

When users ask you to perform tasks, check if any of the available skills match.
When a skill matches the user's request, this is a BLOCKING REQUIREMENT: invoke
the relevant Skill tool BEFORE generating any other response about the task.

A successful Skill invocation (not SkillManage) refills the skill tool-call budget.

Available skills are listed in system-reminder messages in the conversation.

Parameters:
  - skill: The name of the skill to invoke
  - args: Optional arguments to pass to the skill (space-separated)

The skill's instructions will be returned as the tool result. Follow them carefully.

args.description: Optional arguments to pass to the skill. Space-separated values that replace {{arg}} placeholders in the skill content.

skill.description: The name of the skill to invoke. Available skills are listed in system-reminder messages.

tools.name: SkillManage
tools.description:
Create or manage autogenerated skills. SkillManage does not invoke a skill or refill the skill tool-call budget. After creating a skill, invoke it with Skill to refill; a no-mutation review does not refill.

The target library is class-level: prefer enriching an existing umbrella skill
over creating a narrow one-session skill. Preserve specific context in a labeled
SKILL.md subsection or a references/, templates/, scripts/, or assets/ support file.

Actions:
  - create: Create a new class-level umbrella only when no loaded or existing skill covers the workflow. Never overwrite an existing skill.
  - patch: Patch an existing skill immediately when you find it outdated, incomplete, or wrong — don't wait to be asked
  - write_file: Add narrow but valuable context under an existing umbrella skill
  - absorb_files: Carry support files from one skill package into another byte-for-byte. Use this when merging, NOT read_file+write_file.
  - read_file: Read one support file from an existing skill package
  - review: Record a completed review with no mutation when nothing reusable was learned
  - view: Load a skill's full instructions. When you view a skill, follow its instructions for the current task. If the skill needs updating, patch it immediately.
  - history: List immutable package revisions, newest first.
  - undo: Append a revert revision restoring a prior package state.
  - list: See all available skills with name, version, and description
  - archive: Recoverably archive a skill. Supply absorbed_into after consolidation, or pruning_reason when no knowledge was retained.

Parameters:
  - action: "create" | "patch" | "write_file" | "absorb_files" | "read_file" | "review" | "view" | "history" | "undo" | "list" | "archive"
  - name: skill identifier matching ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$ (max 64; "archive" and Windows device aliases are reserved)
  - description: what the skill does (create, patch)
  - instructions: the full skill body (create, patch; configured policy may impose a minimum)
  - append: append patch instructions instead of replacing them
  - tags: comma-separated discovery tags (optional, create)
  - category: organization category (optional, create)
  - file_path/file_content: support file path and content (write_file)
  - from_skill: skill whose support files are being carried across (absorb_files)
  - file_paths: comma-separated support paths to carry; omit to carry every support file (absorb_files)
  - absorbed_into/pruning_reason: archive provenance; one is required
  - dropped_files: comma-separated support paths you deliberately decline to carry, with archive; each must be justified in pruning_reason or the archive is refused
  - review_reason: why no skill mutation is appropriate (review)
  - offset/limit: optional Unicode character range for paged view output
  - expected_revision: revision returned by view; required for existing-skill mutations
  - revision: optional history revision to restore (undo defaults to the prior revision)

absorb_files copies bytes on disk. Use it to preserve bytes and revision tracking when moving a script,
image, or other binary artifact between packages: read_file + write_file routes
the content through the model, which silently rewrites text and cannot represent
binary at all. archive with absorbed_into is refused when the source still has
support files the umbrella does not hold byte-for-byte.

Returns the skill path (create), updated skill info (patch), full skill content (view),
or a listing of all skills (list).

absorbed_into.description: Umbrella skill that absorbed this skill before archive

append.description: Append patch instructions instead of replacing them

dropped_files.description: Comma-separated support paths deliberately not carried forward; requires pruning_reason to justify the loss

expected_revision.description: Current revision returned by view; required for existing-skill mutations

file_path.description: Relative support path under references/, templates/, scripts/, or assets/

file_paths.description: Comma-separated support paths to carry; omit to carry every support file (absorb_files)

from_skill.description: Source skill whose support files are copied into 'name' (absorb_files)

instructions.description: Full skill body; configured policy may impose a minimum

limit.description: For view: maximum Unicode characters returned. For history: maximum revisions returned, newest first (full history when omitted).

name.description: Skill identifier; archive and Windows device aliases are reserved

offset.description: Unicode character offset for paged view output

pruning_reason.description: Why archive is safe when there is no absorption target

review_reason.description: Why the completed review needs no skill mutation

revision.description: Revision to restore (undo; defaults to prior revision)

Use direct tools for small lookups. Launch independent subagents together, without duplicating their work. Use run_in_background for long work; completion is reported automatically, and SubagentOutput retrieves the result. Synchronous output is capped at 8 MB.

tools.name: annoyed
tools.description: Publish an actionable product-friction report after one isolated tool-less ownership consultation. Trebol-owned harness defects route to cloverinternational/trebol; project defects route only to a host-verified active-project GitHub repository. Upstream, non-actionable, uncertain, missing-remote, and judge-failure submissions go to explicit Trebol triage. The transcript remains local and is never published. tools.name: apply_patch
tools.description:
Edit files with a V4A patch. Use it for creating, updating, deleting, or moving files.

*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: relative/or/absolute/path
[*** Move to: new/path]
@@ optional anchor (class/function line) to disambiguate
 context line (space prefix)
-removed line
+added line
 context line
*** Add File: new/file (every body line starts with '+')
*** Delete File: old/file
*** End Patch

Rules: 3 lines of context around each change; use @@ anchors when context repeats; no line numbers. Multiple files may be combined — the patch applies atomically (all operations succeed or none are written).

cwd.description: Optional directory that relative paths in the patch resolve against. Use this to edit a linked git worktree of the same repository when the conversation workspace is pinned to a different checkout. Absolute paths are still permitted when they fall inside that worktree.

input.description: The full patch, from '*** Begin Patch' to '*** End Patch'.

tools.name: bash

Execute a shell command and capture stdout, stderr, exit code, duration, and timeout status. Pipes and redirections are supported.

Set timeout_seconds to a JSON integer for every command; booleans are invalid. Defaults to 90 seconds when missing or malformed; values below the enforced 60-second minimum are raised automatically. Use cwd instead of cd.

tools.name: bootstrap
tools.description:
Gather task-relevant memory, load selected skills, and propose a task plan. Loads at most two relevant skills before planning. Follow returned loadedSkills instructions without reloading them; verify task proposals against the repository before implementation. Tasks are always established and reconciled; an existing focused task is reused instead of creating another graph.

Codemode: `tools.bootstrap(args)` resolves to a string.

replanKey.description: Explicit scope-change identifier for re-decomposition. Reuse the same key on retries; a new key reconciles the live task graph again.

tools.name: codemode
tools.description:
Run JavaScript that calls other tools. The input is raw JavaScript (not JSON, no code fence), run as an async function body in a QuickJS sandbox: top-level `await` and `return` work. No Node, file system, network, or timers.
- `await tools.<name>({ ...args })` resolves to a string, or an object if the tool's declaration says so, and rejects with an Error on failure. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.
- Optional first line: `// @options: {"max_output_tokens": 10000, "timeout_ms": 60000}`

Globals:
- `text(value)`, `image(dataUrlOrImageBlock)`, `console.log(...)`, and top-level `return` add output; `exit()` ends the script. With several text items, each starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` lines follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block. `image()` also saves the image to a temp file and the result names its path.
- `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values across codemode calls.
- `ALL_TOOLS`, `await searchTools(query, { limit?, namespace? })`, `await describeTool(name)`, `await describeNamespace(name)`: find unlisted tools, such as MCP tools.
- `models`: classifiers and image generation. Read /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/codemode.md first.

tools.name: context_remember
tools.description:
Capture indexed knowledge with evidence references; no file needed. Memory records what is known: project architecture, domain facts, terminology, decisions and rationale, constraints, preferences, and relevant ongoing context. A project's established process is knowledge about that project. Reusable instructions for how an agent should investigate, implement, debug, or verify belong in skills, not memory. Separate factual context from procedural advice when an observation contains both. Preserve evidence, uncertainty, and freshness; later corrections may invalidate earlier claims. Do not treat an agent's success claim as verified fact. This index currently uses namespace/workspace/session scope; it does not promote notes to repository or global memory.

Codemode: `tools.context_remember(args)` resolves to a string.
